question.problem:
Given that the log-likelihood function for a particular sample of independent normal random variables is

$$
l(\theta )=-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-8.4+7.4\text{ }\,\theta -6\text{ }\,{\theta }^{2},
$$

what is the maximum likelihood estimate $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}$ from this sample? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
In order to find the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta ,$ we calculate the derivative of the log-likelihood function, set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $\theta .$

First, we take the derivative of $l(\theta ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}l}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-8.4+7.4\text{ }\,\theta -6\text{ }\,{\theta }^{2}) \\  & =7.4-12\text{ }\,\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we set the derivative equal to $0$ and solve for $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}7.4-12\text{ }\,\theta  & =0 \\ 12\text{ }\,\theta  & =7.4 \\ \theta  & ≈0.617\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, for this sample, the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta $ is $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}≈0.617,$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
